account: It is day one, seven in the morning, and I am in my office with the secretary. I have reviewed all four office books. Today's business is office work at eight, grain inspection at the east-bank mill at ten, lunch at home at noon, council letters at thirteen, tea with the neighbour at the dockside cottage at fifteen, office again at sixteen-thirty, a great-hall lighting inspection at eighteen, and home at nineteen. The builder requested the lighting inspection yesterday, said eight lanterns were installed, and intends to return shortly before eighteen to accompany me inside. I approved it, and the secretary has recorded it in an updated appointment book while preserving the original. The older inspection-request book still says approval is pending, but that is superseded by my approval and the updated schedule. The builder was carrying a lantern this morning; that fits his stated lighting work. I have noticed repeated reminders about this inspection, but have no evidence of another purpose. Yesterday the neighbour mentioned vague rumours of bridge or port changes. Neither the neighbour nor the secretary had verified details, and the builder explicitly said he had no such works proposed. I therefore regard that as unconfirmed chatter, not an established project. Yesterday I also saw freight give an emerald to the baker; I do not know what the payment was for. Nothing I have directly observed establishes wrongdoing. My immediate task is to return the four books to their chest and keep today's appointments.
